details: Escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly US-Iran airstrikes, have intensified inflation fears and a "risk-off" sentiment across global markets. This has led to a significant downturn in cryptocurrency prices, with Bitcoin falling below $74,000 and Ethereum below $2,000. Over $900 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in the last 24 hours, primarily from long positions. Rising oil prices are contributing to higher inflation expectations, making investors cautious of volatile assets.
title: Geopolitical Tensions, Inflation Fears Drive Bitcoin Below $74K

details: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams stated that the central bank's monetary policy is "in the right place" given the current outlook. However, he expects inflation to remain high in the near term due to factors like import tax increases and energy shocks from the Middle East conflict, with pressures easing later in the year. Financial markets are closely monitoring upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, GDP revisions, and jobless claims for further economic direction.
title: Fed's Williams: Monetary Policy "In Right Place" Despite Elevated Inflation

details: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced substantial outflows, with approximately $1.7 billion in cumulative outflows over a five-day period as institutional investors reduce exposure. This de-risking is occurring amidst broader macroeconomic uncertainty and rising bond yields, which make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive compared to traditional assets offering real returns.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Outflows as Institutions De-Risk

details: An Irish parliamentary committee has recommended the introduction of greater regulation to protect consumers from the risks of speculative cryptocurrency investments. The committee highlighted concerns about the blurred lines between neobanks and crypto exchanges, suggesting mandates for digital banking apps to provide clear risk warnings for crypto trading services.
title: Irish Parliament Recommends Stricter Crypto Investment Regulations
